NMPolitics.net, August 2, 2006: 'Gov. Bill Richardson has declared a state of disaster in eight counties' (Dona Ana, Grant, Hidalgo, Sandoval, San Miguel, Sierra, Socorro and Valencia) after a week of heavy rain and thunderstorms. The story does not give the day he signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Eastern New Mexico News, March 26, 2007: 'Gov. Bill Richardson declared Clovis a state disaster area Sunday' (March 25) and released $750,000 by executive order, after Friday's tornado.

Insurance Journal (AP), August 11, 2008: 'Richardson has declared Lincoln and Otero counties disaster areas' after the July 27 flood from the remnants of Hurricane Dolly. The story does not give the day he signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Mountain Mail (Socorro), August 19, 2010: the Governor signed the disaster order on Tuesday, August 17, for flood damage after heavy rains in late July and early August.
KRWG, February 3, 2011: Gov. Susana Martinez 'has declared a state of emergency' after thousands lost natural gas service in the bitter cold that began Tuesday, February 1.
Los Alamos Daily Post, reprinting Executive Order 2013-029, signed July 30, 2013: 'declaring an emergency throughout New Mexico due to the severe storms and flooding across the state in July'.

Los Alamos Daily Post, reprinting Executive Order 2013-031: 'do hereby declare a State of Disaster to exist in state of New Mexico due to flooding', with the emergency period starting September 9, 2013. The order as printed carries no signing date; the Associated Press reported Gov. Martinez declared the emergency on Friday, September 13, 2013 (https://www.fox13now.com/2013/09/13/new-mexico-floods-hundreds-evacuated-governor-declares-emergency).

The Governor's executive order list (captured November 10, 2016 by the End of Term web archive) gives Executive Order 2011-075, 'Declaring a disaster in Sandoval County due to flooding.', dated Friday, August 26, 2011.

The Governor's executive order list (captured November 10, 2016 by the End of Term web archive) gives Executive Order 2012-018, 'Declaring an Emergency Throughout New Mexico Due to Enhanced Flood Potential Caused by Severe Wildfires', dated Monday, June 18, 2012. Signed four days before the June 22 flooding it anticipated; counted because it names the flood hazard and was in force when the flooding began.

KSFR, August 7, 2014: Gov. Martinez 'has issued an executive order that provides up to 750-thousand dollars in emergency aid' for recent flooding; 'The emergency declaration on Wednesday also authorizes the use of National Guard troops'. Wednesday is August 6, 2014.

National Guard, September 24, 2014: 'Martinez signed Executive Order 2014-015 early last week declaring an emergency across the state.' The report does not give the day, so the row carries the date of the report.

Claims Journal, May 4, 2004, reporting Governor Richardson's announcement that the White House had approved federal disaster assistance 'for the four New Mexico counties that experienced extensive damage from severe storms earlier last month' (Eddy, Mora, San Miguel and Bernalillo): 'The Governor previously had declared these counties eligible for state disaster assistance.' The story does not give the day he declared, so the row carries the date of the report and is compared on April 2, 2004, the first day of the federal declaration's incident period (DR-1514, April 2 to 11, 2004).

Associated Press report from Ruidoso in the Deseret News of Tuesday, May 9, 2000 ('Wildfires force hundreds in N.M. to flee'): 'The state is a tinderbox,' Gov. Gary Johnson said in declaring a state of emergency Monday. Monday was May 8, 2000, and the row carries that day. The story covers the Cerro Grande fire, a National Park Service prescribed burn at Bandelier National Monument that got out of control near Los Alamos, and a fire started by a campfire in Gavilan Canyon near Ruidoso; it does not say whether the emergency covered the whole state or only some counties. It matches DR-1329 (Cerro Grande fire, May 5 to June 9, 2000) and EM-3154 (fire threats, May 5 to July 7, 2000).
